fluff.overview: During the heyday of the Star League, Andurien Aerotek and Imstar Aerospace, both notable Free Worlds-based aerospace companies, debuted conventional fighters that became standards known far and wide across human-occupied space. Not to be outdone, the Federated Suns claimed a piece of that same military niche when Jalastar Aerospace of Panpour introduced its for-export conventional fighter concept, the Meteor Heavy Strike Fighter. Rather than mimicking the aggressive international sales approach used by its Free Worlds competitors, Jalastar took a more direct marketing strategy and aimed their strike fighter at customers in the Terran Hegemony, a decision that would ultimately shape the Meteor's distribution across the Inner Sphere for centuries to come.
fluff.capabilities:
Though it has become the standard by which heavy strike fighters are defined, the Meteor, like Andurien Aerotek's Angel, is unusual for its fusion-based design, which saved tonnage but produced a higher initial price tag. Price was only a minor concern to Hegemony buyers when the Meteor debuted, and the asking price allowed Jalastar to provide a fighter with respectable airspeed and maneuverability while leaving room for heavy weapons and respectable armor for a conventional fighter.

The centerpiece of the Meteor's arsenal is its nose-mounted Mydron B heavy autocannon, boasting two tons of munitions for sustained medium-range firepower. A single hit from the weapon can down most conventional fighters and even cripple lighter aerospace fighters foolish enough to tempt their fate against it. Backing this weapon is a pair of wing-mounted Holly SRM 4 packs, particularly ideal in anti-ground attack runs against vehicles or when targeting low-flying VTOLs. Even with this formidable array, most Meteors were often billed as bomber-fighters and frequently flew into battle laden with enough external ordnance to threaten small concentrations of ground forces, including BattleMek and armor companies.
fluff.deployment: Jalastar's Terran-directed marketing campaign ended up having the same effect on Meteor sales as Andurien Aerotek's and Imstar Aerospace's Sphere-wide approach did with the Angel and Defender strike fighters. Third-party sales prior to the fall of the Star League saw the Meteor exported to planetary garrisons across human-occupied space. When the Star League fell, the Great Houses claimed scores of these fighters as each seized its respective slice of Hegemony territory. The widely available specs allowed for a boom in homegrown production, making the Meteor the template by which all heavy strike fighters would be known.
fluff.history:
House Kurita produced both a carbon copy Meteor, dubbed the Inseki ("Meteorite"), and an after-market upgrade variant, the Inseki II, that took full advantage of the fusion plant by trading the fighter's weapons for a nose-mounted Hellstar PPC, a pair of wing-mounted Telos DecaCluster LRM 10 racks, and a tail-mounted machine gun to deter close pursuit. The Taurian Concordat produced the Bat Hawk variant, using a locally manufactured 225-rated turbine engine in place of the more expensive fusion plant while retaining the nose-mounted heavy autocannon. The wing-mounted SRMs were deleted in favor of the heavier engine and replaced by a single nose-mounted Harvester SRM twin-pack.

In 3060, Gutierrez Aerospace on Trellisane introduced a Free Worlds-made upgrade of the Meteor designated the Meteor-G. Made available for export sale despite misgivings among the Free Worlds League's LCCC, this variant trades the older Mydron Model B for a Corean Light Gauss Rifle and replaces the Holly 4 packs with more efficient Guided Technologies 2nd Gen Streak SRM 4 launchers. These changes forced the designers to reduce the Meteor-G's range by one third.

The Federated Suns also fielded an upgraded variant known as the Meteor-U, which upgrades the Mydron B to an Ultra series and replaces each wing-mounted SRM launcher with a pair of Intek medium lasers, adding two heat sinks to handle the load. Like the Meteor-G, this variant sacrifices endurance but nearly doubles its offensive punch in combat.
